issues.problem: Feedback for the distractor 'Put the database next to the public portal in the screened subnet' says: 'A screened subnet is safer than the internal LAN, but still the wrong place for the core database.' That is backwards. A screened subnet is the more exposed zone (it holds internet-reachable services); the internal network is the more protected one. The sentence teaches the opposite of the section's own zone descriptions.
issues.fix: Replace the feedback with: "A screened subnet holds internet-facing services, so it is more exposed than the internal network. The core database does not belong there."

issues.problem: The item 'Multicloud analytics' (two public providers, no on-premises part) is filed under the zone 'Hybrid environment - Connected mix of on-prem and cloud resources'. That contradicts the same section's first link ('Hybrid and multicloud are not the same'), the Pocket Note sec.cloud-models, and xf.sec.cloud-models.multi, all of which define hybrid as on-premises plus cloud and multicloud as several providers. The map shows multicloud as a kind of hybrid while the text says it is not.
issues.fix: Rename the zone so both items fit: {id:"hybrid",name:"Mixed environments",desc:"Workloads spread across on-premises and cloud, or across more than one cloud provider"}. Keep items 'hyb' and 'multi' in it. Also change the third practice option from 'Only the hybrid zone' to 'Mixed environments' with feedback: "Mixing sites or providers describes where workloads sit, not event-driven execution with no servers to patch."

issues.id: sec.cloud-models (lines[2], card c1) + data-lessons-sec-2.js lesson 20 map links[0]
issues.problem: Hybrid is defined only as 'on-prem and cloud', and the lesson states flatly that hybrid and multicloud are not the same. The source this batch cites (Professor Messer, Cloud Infrastructures, 3.1) defines hybrid cloud as using multiple clouds across different providers, and NIST SP 800-145 defines it as a composition of two or more distinct cloud infrastructures (private, community, or public). SY0-701 lists 'Hybrid considerations' under 3.1 and 'Multi-cloud systems' under 3.4, so a learner can meet a multi-provider scenario where 'hybrid' is the expected answer. The app's definition is the common industry one and is not wrong, but it is stated more absolutely than the sources support.
issues.fix: lines[2]: "Hybrid combines distinct environments, usually on-premises or private cloud with public cloud; multicloud uses several providers." Card c1 answer: "A mix of two or more distinct environments, most often on-premises or private cloud combined with public cloud." Lesson 20 map links[0]: "Hybrid usually means on-premises or private cloud combined with public cloud, while multicloud means more than one provider. Some courses call any mix of several clouds hybrid, so read the scenario's wording."

issues.problem: All three yes/no items in this file (xf.sec.ot.yn, xf.sec.secure-comms.yn, xf.sec.targets.yn) use the identical pattern true, true, false, and in each the false row is an absurd statement ('expose it directly to the internet for visibility'). A learner can score the whole type by pattern alone.
issues.fix: Use rows in this order (false, true, true): ["A real-time operating system is chosen mainly because it runs a wider range of general-purpose applications than a desktop OS.",false,"An RTOS is chosen for deterministic, predictable timing, not for broad application support."], ["ICS and SCADA environments often prioritize availability over frequent change windows.",true,"Outages can affect physical processes, so uptime often outweighs frequent patch cycles."], ["When an embedded or OT device cannot be patched easily, isolating or segmenting it is a common compensating control.",true,"Hard-to-patch devices are usually isolated and tightly segmented to reduce exposure."]

issues.problem: Same true, true, false pattern as the other two yes/no items, and the false row ('SASE is mainly a battery technology') can be rejected with no knowledge.
issues.fix: Use rows (false, true, false): ["IPsec transport mode is the usual choice for site-to-site VPNs because it wraps the entire original packet inside a new one.",false,"That describes tunnel mode. Transport mode protects only the payload and keeps the original IP header."], ["A forward proxy typically relays requests on behalf of clients rather than protecting public web applications from injection attacks.",true,"Client-side relay and policy are proxy functions; injection defense for web apps is a WAF function."], ["SD-WAN on its own provides the cloud-delivered security services that define SASE.",false,"SD-WAN handles WAN path selection. SASE combines networking with cloud-delivered security and access controls."]

issues.problem: Same true, true, false pattern as the other two yes/no items; the false row is worded so strongly ('alone removes the need for backups') that it gives itself away.
issues.fix: Use rows (true, false, true): ["If leadership says a system may lose no more than one hour of data, they are defining RPO.",true,"RPO measures acceptable data loss as a time window."], ["A generator bridges the first seconds of a power failure, and a UPS then carries the site through a long outage.",false,"It is the other way round: the UPS bridges the short gap and the generator supplies long-term power while it has fuel."], ["Clustering and load balancing keep a service up when a server fails, but they do not bring back data that was deleted or corrupted.",true,"Availability reduces downtime from component failure; recovering lost data still needs backups."]

issues.problem: The stem asks about 'hybrid or multicloud' and the two correct options are the only ones that start with 'Hybrid' and 'Multicloud'. The distractors use 'always' and 'means the same thing as', which are easy to reject.
issues.fix: Replace o[2] and o[3] with: "Hybrid means every workload runs with one public provider" and "Multicloud means one provider hosting several customers on shared hardware". Update why to: "Hybrid mixes environments, while multicloud mixes providers. A single public provider is neither, and several customers on shared hardware describes multitenancy."

issues.problem: Distractors 'A jump server is the same thing as a firewall' and 'TLS replaces the need for any traffic filtering' are absolute statements nobody would pick; the item can be answered without knowing what a WAF or NGFW does.
issues.fix: Replace o[2] and o[3] with: "A stateful firewall judges each packet with no record of the connection it belongs to" and "An IDS on a mirror port can drop malicious packets before they arrive". Update why to: "WAFs protect web apps and NGFWs inspect applications, not only ports. Stateful firewalls do track connections, and an out-of-band IDS can only alert."

issues.problem: Each match item has exactly one extra option and it comes from an unrelated topic (Air gap, Cold site, Load balancing). The extra is obvious, so the last pair is always found by elimination. No extra fits a row, so the keys themselves are correct.
issues.fix: Add a second, same-topic extra to each: containers.match extra:["Air gap","Software-defined networking"]; zones.match extra:["Cold site","Forward proxy"]; protection.match extra:["Load balancing","Hashing"]. None of the added extras fits any existing row.

issues.problem: All three distractors are things no one would do (install features from the internet, move controllers into serverless, replace controllers with a SaaS app). The correct option is also the longest.
issues.fix: o:["Isolate the controllers on a segmented industrial network","Schedule monthly patch reboots for the controllers","Install the office endpoint agent on each controller","Move the controllers onto the office VLAN for monitoring"]; no:["Monthly reboots conflict with the yearly shutdown window and the need to stay online.","Controllers often cannot run standard endpoint agents, and an agent does not remove the path from the office LAN.","Sharing the office VLAN gives office malware a direct path to the controllers."]

issues.problem: Distractors all make exposure obviously worse or are unrelated (public web server on the control VLAN, containers for billing, internet patch checks).
issues.fix: o:["Remove the path and isolate the control network","Keep the route and add an IDS to watch it","Run weekly vulnerability scans of the controllers from the billing network","Give billing administrators accounts on the pump controllers"]; no:["An IDS only alerts; the unnecessary path between billing and control would still exist.","Scanning from the billing network is the kind of outside scanning the control network cannot tolerate.","More accounts widen casual admin access instead of removing the path."]

issues.problem: Distractors (more VLANs, a cold site, replacing TLS with IPsec) are not execution models at all, so only one option answers the question asked.
issues.fix: o:["Use a serverless function","Run an always-on virtual machine that waits for uploads","Deploy a container cluster the team sizes and patches","Add the task to the on-premises web server"]; no:["An always-on VM still has to be patched and sized, and it sits idle between uploads.","A self-managed cluster keeps the patching and sizing work the team wants to avoid.","An on-premises server is still a server to patch and size for idle periods."]

issues.problem: Distractors (hot site, tokenization, reverse proxy 'for every laptop') are unrelated to network admission.
issues.fix: o:["802.1X on the switch ports","A screened subnet for the classroom switches","An IDS on a mirror port","A forward proxy for classroom web traffic"]; no:["A screened subnet separates public-facing services; it does not authenticate devices that plug in.","An IDS alerts on suspicious traffic after a device is already connected.","A forward proxy filters web requests but does not stop a device from joining the network."]

issues.problem: Distractors (cold site, 802.1X on laptops, site-to-site VPN) have nothing to do with inspecting web requests, and the correct option is the longest.
issues.fix: o:["A web application firewall","A packet-filtering rule that allows only TCP 443","An IDS on a mirror port","A forward proxy for staff browsing"]; no:["The site already allows only HTTPS; a port rule cannot see attacks inside permitted web requests.","An IDS could alert on the attempts, but it would not block them.","A forward proxy filters outbound staff browsing, not inbound requests to the public site."]

issues.problem: Distractors (cold site replication, 802.1X, air-gapped networking) are not remote-access architectures. The item never makes the learner separate SASE from SD-WAN or a VPN, which is the distinction the exam tests.
issues.fix: o:["SASE","SD-WAN only","A site-to-site IPsec VPN to headquarters","A jump server at headquarters"]; no:["SD-WAN optimizes WAN paths between sites but does not by itself deliver the cloud security services described.","A site-to-site VPN links fixed sites and still hauls traffic through headquarters.","A jump server is an admin path into a protected zone, not an access architecture for all remote staff."]

issues.problem: The correct option hedges across two labels ('highly sensitive or restricted') while the distractors are joke answers (public marketing content, disposable test data, guest resource).
issues.fix: o:["Restricted, with access limited to the named legal team","Internal, open to any employee of the firm","Public, because the merger will be announced eventually","Left unlabeled until the deal closes"]; no:["Firm-wide access is broader than the small legal team the scenario allows.","A future announcement does not make the drafts public today; disclosure now would cause major harm.","Unlabeled data gets no handling rules, the opposite of what high-impact data needs."]

issues.problem: Distractors (another load balancer, lowering classification labels, disabling backup encryption) are unrelated or self-evidently harmful.
issues.fix: o:["Run recovery and restore tests","Increase the backups from nightly to hourly","Add a second off-site copy of the backups","Hold a tabletop discussion of the recovery plan"]; no:["More frequent backups reduce data loss but still do not prove a restore works.","Another copy adds redundancy, not evidence that systems can be rebuilt in time.","A tabletop walks through the plan on paper; it does not show the backups restore within the required time."]

notes: Read every item in all five files: 17 concepts (34 recall cards), 4 comparisons, 27 scenarios, 3 lessons (levels 20-22: 15 content sections with practice plus 3 'check' sections that only draw from the scenario pool), 12 exam-style items. Structure is clean: every scenario has no.length == options-1 and each `no` entry lines up with its option; every practice has exactly one correct option; dd first options, multi first-n options, match pairs and yn truth values are all correct; no match `extra` fits a row; cmp:'cmp.rto-rpo' resolves to data-cn-compare.js; tools/check-content.js passes. data-cn-sec-2-cmp.js has no issues. No keyed answer is wrong, and I found no scored question with a second defensible answer. Level 19 (review casebook) is not in the listed files; it is in data-lessons-sec-1.js and covers domains 1-2. I read it (6 cases, keys correct, one giveaway issue logged) but did not source-check the batch 1 concepts it links to. The batch contains no port numbers, RAID levels, backup-type or MTTR/MTBF content, so there was nothing of that kind to verify; the only figures are scenario RTO/RPO values. Coverage gaps against the objectives (not errors, not logged as issues): 3.2 has nothing on UTM, layer 4 vs layer 7, EAP, sensors, reverse proxy, active/passive and inline/tap device attributes, and no note defining fail-open/fail-closed; 3.3 omits hashing, obfuscation, segmentation, data sovereignty, trade secrets and human/non-human-readable data; 3.4 omits platform diversity, continuity of operations, capacity planning, geographic dispersion, test types (tabletop, failover, simulation, parallel processing), backup details (onsite/offsite, frequency, snapshots, replication, journaling) and UPS/generator in the Pocket Notes (lesson 22 covers power briefly). Professor Messer pages were read through a summarising fetch tool, so quotations from them are the tool's extraction, not text I saw verbatim; direct HTTP checks of the URLs were blocked by the sandbox proxy. The CompTIA objectives PDF was not fetched; objective placement of RTO/RPO (5.2) and multi-cloud (3.4) is taken from Messer's course index and my knowledge of the SY0-701 objectives.
